_note: American English. Deliberately close to en-gb — this copy has few spelling divergences — but WhatsApp itself says 'voice message' in the US, and that is the term users will look for. Where en-gb and en-us would be identical the key is still carried, so the locale is complete rather than half-falling-back.
title: Transcribe — VoiceDebrief (beta)
metaDescription: Drop in a voice message or an audio recording and get a transcript, a debrief, and an infographic in one pass — everything runs in your browser with your own OpenRouter key.
heroHeading: Drop in your voice message. That's it.
heroLeadHtml: Transcript, summary and an infographic in one pass — everything runs in this browser. Beta: bring your own OpenRouter key.
samplesLabel: no voice message handy? try a sample:
findNoteSummary: where do I find my voice message?
findNoteBodyHtml: Laptop: open WhatsApp Web/Desktop → the voice message → download (.opus). Android: share/export the message (.opus/.ogg). iPhone: forwarding between apps produces .m4a — that works too.

translateWhy: The transcript always stays in the language spoken. The summary and infographic are built from the translation.

keyGuideLink: How do I get a key? — five steps, and how to cap what it can spend
demoTry: ▶ see it work — no key needed
demoNote: This is a scripted example, not a real recording. Nothing was sent anywhere and nothing was charged.
routingHonest: Your audio and its transcript are sent to OpenRouter, which passes them to a model provider. We do not know which provider handles your recording, and we have no control over what they do with it. Do not use this for anything you would not hand to a third party.
modelCaveat: Written by a model, not a stenographer. It can mishear, and it can add words nobody said. Check anything that matters against the audio.
